subject: divorced dads
one_liner: A relationship platform for men re-entering the market with a 60/40 custody split and a brand-new mattress.
brand_voice_notes: Deadpan HR-gentle sincerity. The platform is extremely careful with the user and it reads as unsettling. Never jokes about the marriage or the ex; the jokes live in lamps, air fryers, kayaks, greige paint, custody calendars, and the phrase 'in a really good place.' Prices stated with total confidence. Institutional kindness as a product surface.

hero.sub: Threshold matches recently divorced men with people who understand that the first four photos are from 2019. He's in a really good place right now. Serious inquiries only.

features.title: Custody-Aware Matching
features.blurb: Our scheduling engine ingests your parenting calendar and suppresses all matches on kid weekends. Dates are proposed only for Saturdays you were already going to spend at the driving range.

features.title: Verified Apartment
features.blurb: A Threshold field agent inspects your new place and certifies a minimum of one lamp, one shower curtain, and one pan that isn't nonstick-flaking. The badge is stitched onto your profile in institutional green.

features.title: Prompt Assist
features.blurb: Machine-written answers to profile prompts, trained on 40,000 men who are doing great, actually. Mentions the gym once, the kids twice, and the divorce zero times.

demo_screen_concept: A swipeable card stack titled 'This weekend's market': divorced-dad profiles as heritage membership cards. Each card carries a portrait, name and age, a months-since-finalized counter, stitched merit badges (Verified Apartment, Lamp Count: 3, Air Fryer Owner), a free-weekend overlap meter showing custody-schedule compatibility as a percentage, and one profile prompt answer. Drag or swipe left/right, or use the buttons: pass ('Not ready') and like ('Seems ready'). A top bar shows the user's next free weekend and a running 'Doing Great' streak counter.

design_direction.style: Heritage workwear catalog crossed with a lodge membership handbook, cream daylight mode. The page is staged as the consumer site of a heavily funded relationship company that has decided the recently divorced man is a heritage asset in need of re-certification and files starting over under outfitting. A warm cream canvas ground (#F7F2E7) runs the whole page with no gradients and no texture washes; structure comes from catalog print chrome: 2px walnut-ink borders, near-square 6px radii, thin double rules under section headings, and small-caps wide-tracked catalog labels (DEPT. 02 / PROVISIONS), so every panel reads as a page from a fall outfitter catalog rather than a website. The core motif is the embroidered merit patch: oval and shield badges drawn in CSS/SVG with a 2px solid border wrapped by an inner 1px dashed stitch line, awarded for domestic milestones (VERIFIED APARTMENT, LAMP COUNT 3, OWNS A PAN) and used as tier seals, list bullets, and the hero crest. The second motif is the stitch rule: 1px dashed divider lines in thread tan that hem sections and card edges like flannel seams. One forest green (#2F5D42) carries the wordmark crest, every primary CTA, and the certified patch fills; one rationed ember rust (#C1502E) is reserved for the highlighted word per headline, in-progress inspection states, and the live 'doing great' streak dot, and appears nowhere else. Besley sets the wordmark and headlines in heavy Clarendon-style slab serif with hardware-store-est.-1892 confidence; Work Sans carries plain, faintly onboarding-packet body copy. Every figure that pretends to be re-entry telemetry (months since finalized, lamp counts, overlap percentages, tier prices) is set in Courier Prime with tabular figures inside thin-ruled cream wells, so it reads like the inspection form, not marketing. Motion is catalog-restrained: patches tilt 2 degrees on hover with the stitch line tightening, cards lift 2px with the border deepening, CTAs depress 1px on press, the streak dot pulses on a 4s cycle, sections fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur, no clay shadow pairs, no bento lattice, no didone engraving, no HUD brackets, no nautical chrome, no storefront capsules, no sticker offset shadows, no emoji. Reads like a company that files grief under 'seasonal outfitting' and considers the floor lamp a load-bearing document.
